themes.disagreements: Causal forest support for effect modification is low for both (26% for OA, 20% for osteopenia), confirming their roles as primarily confounders rather than effect modifiers.
themes.interpretation: High-confidence signals for both treatment assignment and outcome prognosis, suggesting a strong confounding role.
themes.name: Bone Density and Musculoskeletal Comorbidities

themes.disagreements: Optic chiasm enhancement shows strong prognostic (66%) and interaction (53%) signals, whereas optic nerve enhancement signals are weak and inconsistent across models.
themes.interpretation: Radiological signals associated with the optic pathway showing a blend of prognostic importance and treatment-heterogeneity evidence.
themes.name: Optic Pathway Imaging Enhancement

themes.disagreements: NYHA class is primarily an effect modifier (60% Causal Forest), while organomegaly is a stronger predictor of treatment (60%) and outcome (73%), marking it as a confounder.
themes.interpretation: Indicators of overall patient health and organ involvement, demonstrating either strong prognosis or effect modification.
themes.name: Systemic Clinical and Functional Status

themes.disagreements: While some features show moderate predictive forest support, these are not replicated across other model families and lack the strength to justify a specific role.
themes.interpretation: General patient characteristics and clinical status with insufficient or contradictory evidence to establish a causal role.
themes.name: Demographic and Operational Factors
